iOS · Wisconsin Creative · Notifications Slice 3

Notification Levels on iOS

Profile → Notifications is where people tune what reaches their phone. It used to offer one on/off switch per type; it now offers Off, Silent, or Standard per type, recurring quiet hours, and more ways to pause.

Side by side

Same fixture scenario (notifications, Staff user, pause active), same iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator, dark appearance, default text size. The after fixture also carries the new server fields (role catalog, levels, quiet hours) the screen now reads. The simulator clock is live, so the pause end time differs by the 15 minutes between runs.

Top of screen

Status, pause, and the new quiet hours.

What changed, and why

On/off became Off, Silent, or Standard

Was

A switch per type. Muting schedule chatter meant losing it entirely.

Now

A menu per type. Silent keeps the alert in Notification Center without sound or lighting the screen; Off also stops that type's email.

Quiet hours

Was

Only a one-off pause, which silenced everything, including overdue gear.

Now

A weekly window in Central Time. Alerts still arrive, silently; overdue-gear alerts can break through.

Types follow the account's role

Was

The same seven types for everyone, hard-coded in the app.

Now

The server sends the types this role actually receives, so staff see item reports and admins see review requests, and new types need no app release.

More ways to pause

Was

1 hour, 1 day, or 1 week.

Now

Adds until tomorrow morning (7 AM) and a custom end time up to 30 days out.

Saves send only the change

Was

Every toggle re-sent the whole preference record.

Now

Each change sends only that field; time-wheel edits are batched into one save. Against an older server the screen falls back to the previous switches.

Verification

  • npm run ios:xcode:verify on the iPhone 18 Pro Max (isolated worktree): XcodeGen drift, simulator build, full XCTest suite, generic device build — passed
  • NotificationPreferenceLevelTests (patch encoding, explicit null resume, tolerant level decoding, Central-time round trip, tomorrow morning) — 5 of 5 passed
  • NotificationSettingsScreenshotUITests on the iPhone 18 Pro Max — before and after both passed; inputs recorded in the hash-bound receipts
  • iOS source-contract tests for notifications, settings, and the API model — 112 passed
  • npx tsc --noEmit clean; npm run verify:docs current
  • Full vitest: the only failures are 11 Schedule contract files broken by a concurrent, uncommitted Schedule refactor; all 15 pass in the worktree without it

Things to know

  • Both sides show a 'requested item could not be found' row. That's the fixture harness answering a background reload with a 404, not part of this change.
  • After-only frames further down the screen: raw/after-scrolled-2.png and raw/after-bottom.png (grouped types and the email-only item-report switch). The before capture has no matching frames.
  • The after capture was built in an isolated worktree of HEAD plus this work only, because a concurrent Schedule refactor in the main checkout does not compile yet.
  • Fixture captures prove layout only. Saving against a live server, APNs silent delivery, and quiet-hours timing still need a signed-in run against dev:preview and the physical iPhone.
  • Not in this slice: opening this screen from the iOS Settings link, a settings shortcut in the inbox, and the /settings/notifications deep link.
